Are the United States and Its Allies Learning Quickly Enough from the War in Ukraine?
news.summary_en: Drawing on more than 30 trips to Ukraine and his experience commanding SAG-U and NSATU, LTG (Ret.) Curtis Buzzard argues that the United States and its allies are not learning from the war fast enough—and the side that adapts faster will hold the edge in future conflicts.

news.title: The Largest Crypto Heist in History Could Have Been Avoided
news.summary_en: North Korea pulled off the largest heist in history, stealing $6 billion from crypto exchange Binance. What will it take for policymakers to wake up to these threats?

news.title: The 2027 Congress and the Dangerous Data Breach Pileup
news.summary_en: The next Congress has an opportunity for bipartisan oversight, legislation, and support to public servants by ensuring mitigations of the multiple, serious data breaches that have recently impacted the executive branch.

news.title: European Nations State Their Vision for the Future of European Security
news.summary_en: A group of 40 European states making up the vast majority of the continent just adopted the “Declaration on key principles of European security.” Europeans are proactively putting on the record their vision of security, pushing back on Russia.

news.title: Resilience and Reform: U.S.-China Relations and the Global Economic Order
news.summary_en: In this collection of survey results and essays from the U.S.-China Global Economic Order (GEO) Dialogue, participants examine how Chinese and international experts view the trade truce, export controls, WTO reform, and the future of the global economy.

news.title: Foreign Policy in the American Heartland: Issues for the 120th Congress
news.summary_en: A new CSIS survey on U.S. foreign policy with registered voters across seven battleground states provides fresh insights into the preferences of a group that could determine the future direction of American foreign policy more than any other group of voters.

news.title: Assessing Nigeria's Efforts to protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt
news.summary_en: Counterterrorism successes do not, by themselves, establish that vulnerable communities are consistently safer. There is not yet sufficient evidence that the underlying problems of prevention, state capacity, accountability, and impunity have been adequately addressed.
